sources.title: Baby on the Way? Here’s How To Prepare Siblings for Their Arrival
sources.quote: Talk with your child about what they were like as a baby and show them photos from their babyhood to give them a sense of what babies do (and don’t do). ... Newborn babies don’t exactly make the most compelling company for toddlers, so it helps if they know something about what to expect long before the baby arrives. ... Make sure your child knows that you’ll be away when the baby comes and that they’ll be well cared for when you’re gone. ... Or let them choose a coming-home outfit for their sibling. ... Allowing your older child to pick out a special gift for the baby. And giving them something special “from the baby.” ... Fetching diapers, burp cloths and other small items. ... Allow your child to keep special toys or stuffed animals that are ‘just for them.’ ... reassure the older child that you have enough love for them and the new baby.
sources.supports: Photos of their own babyhood and what to expect, knowing who cares for them, choosing an outfit, a gift from the baby, small baby jobs, keeping special toys and reassurance of love. A US academic medical centre page, applied to Israeli families as general child health advice.

הוא קטן מאוד, ולא עושה כלום,
בדיוק כמו בתמונות שהראית לי.

את שואלת אם אני רוצה להביא חיתול.

sources.title: Baby on the Way? Here’s How To Prepare Siblings for Their Arrival
sources.quote: Talk with your child about what they were like as a baby and show them photos from their babyhood to give them a sense of what babies do (and don’t do). ... Newborn babies don’t exactly make the most compelling company for toddlers, so it helps if they know something about what to expect long before the baby arrives. ... Make sure your child knows that you’ll be away when the baby comes and that they’ll be well cared for when you’re gone. ... Or let them choose a coming-home outfit for their sibling. ... Allowing your older child to pick out a special gift for the baby. And giving them something special “from the baby.” ... Fetching diapers, burp cloths and other small items. ... Allow your child to keep special toys or stuffed animals that are ‘just for them.’ ... reassure the older child that you have enough love for them and the new baby.
sources.supports: Photos of their own babyhood and what to expect, knowing who cares for them, choosing an outfit, a gift from the baby, small baby jobs, keeping special toys and reassurance of love. A US academic medical centre page, applied to Israeli families as general child health advice.

sources.title: Baby on the Way? Here’s How To Prepare Siblings for Their Arrival
sources.quote: Talk with your child about what they were like as a baby and show them photos from their babyhood to give them a sense of what babies do (and don’t do). ... Newborn babies don’t exactly make the most compelling company for toddlers, so it helps if they know something about what to expect long before the baby arrives. ... Make sure your child knows that you’ll be away when the baby comes and that they’ll be well cared for when you’re gone. ... Or let them choose a coming-home outfit for their sibling. ... Allowing your older child to pick out a special gift for the baby. And giving them something special “from the baby.” ... Fetching diapers, burp cloths and other small items. ... Allow your child to keep special toys or stuffed animals that are ‘just for them.’ ... reassure the older child that you have enough love for them and the new baby.
sources.supports: Photos of their own babyhood and what to expect, knowing who cares for them, choosing an outfit, a gift from the baby, small baby jobs, keeping special toys and reassurance of love. A US academic medical centre page, applied to Israeli families as general child health advice.

sources.title: Make the most of reading with wrigglers
sources.publisher: State Library of Queensland, First 5 Forever (4 May 2021)
sources.quote: Wriggling, or even wandering off does not mean children are not engaged or didn’t get value from sharing stories with you. ... Just talking about the pictures still builds early literacy! ... Even if your child looks busy doing something else, they are still taking in words, sounds and are aware that you’re sharing the story. ... Letting children choose the book can boost their interest and increase their confidence. ... Don’t keep reading to the end just for the sake of it. You can skip pages or just use the pictures and tell your own story. ... Reading with young children is not only about language and sounds but also about building positive experiences with books, and you! ... Sitting still and reading every word will hopefully all come later.
sources.supports: Wriggling and wandering off is natural, the child still takes in the words, choosing the book, skipping pages and talking about the pictures, and reading as a positive experience. An Australian state library page, applied to Israeli families as general early literacy advice.

sources.title: Supporting Language and Literacy Skills from 12–24 Months
sources.quote: Since toddlers are very active, they may only be able to stay still for a story for a few minutes. ... Follow your child’s lead and let her decide which books to read. ... Let your child hold the book and turn the pages. ... Sometimes your child may get up and play with other toys while listening to a story. ... The good news is that while toddlers may run off, they will often return to the story many, many times. ... Children learn through repetition. ... young children need to hear the same story many times to fully understand it.

sources.title: Make the most of reading with wrigglers
sources.publisher: State Library of Queensland, First 5 Forever (4 May 2021)
sources.quote: Wriggling, or even wandering off does not mean children are not engaged or didn’t get value from sharing stories with you. ... Just talking about the pictures still builds early literacy! ... Even if your child looks busy doing something else, they are still taking in words, sounds and are aware that you’re sharing the story. ... Letting children choose the book can boost their interest and increase their confidence. ... Don’t keep reading to the end just for the sake of it. You can skip pages or just use the pictures and tell your own story. ... Reading with young children is not only about language and sounds but also about building positive experiences with books, and you! ... Sitting still and reading every word will hopefully all come later.
sources.supports: Wriggling and wandering off is natural, the child still takes in the words, choosing the book, skipping pages and talking about the pictures, and reading as a positive experience. An Australian state library page, applied to Israeli families as general early literacy advice.

sources.title: Supporting Language and Literacy Skills from 12–24 Months
sources.quote: Since toddlers are very active, they may only be able to stay still for a story for a few minutes. ... Follow your child’s lead and let her decide which books to read. ... Let your child hold the book and turn the pages. ... Sometimes your child may get up and play with other toys while listening to a story. ... The good news is that while toddlers may run off, they will often return to the story many, many times. ... Children learn through repetition. ... young children need to hear the same story many times to fully understand it.
sources.supports: A few minutes at a time, the child choosing, holding the book and turning pages, getting up and coming back, and repeating the same story. Read through a text extraction of the page; quotes are the fragments it returned.

sources.title: Make the most of reading with wrigglers
sources.publisher: State Library of Queensland, First 5 Forever (4 May 2021)
sources.quote: Wriggling, or even wandering off does not mean children are not engaged or didn’t get value from sharing stories with you. ... Just talking about the pictures still builds early literacy! ... Even if your child looks busy doing something else, they are still taking in words, sounds and are aware that you’re sharing the story. ... Letting children choose the book can boost their interest and increase their confidence. ... Don’t keep reading to the end just for the sake of it. You can skip pages or just use the pictures and tell your own story. ... Reading with young children is not only about language and sounds but also about building positive experiences with books, and you! ... Sitting still and reading every word will hopefully all come later.
sources.supports: Wriggling and wandering off is natural, the child still takes in the words, choosing the book, skipping pages and talking about the pictures, and reading as a positive experience. An Australian state library page, applied to Israeli families as general early literacy advice.

sources.title: Supporting Language and Literacy Skills from 12–24 Months
sources.quote: Since toddlers are very active, they may only be able to stay still for a story for a few minutes. ... Follow your child’s lead and let her decide which books to read. ... Let your child hold the book and turn the pages. ... Sometimes your child may get up and play with other toys while listening to a story. ... The good news is that while toddlers may run off, they will often return to the story many, many times. ... Children learn through repetition. ... young children need to hear the same story many times to fully understand it.
sources.supports: A few minutes at a time, the child choosing, holding the book and turning pages, getting up and coming back, and repeating the same story. Read through a text extraction of the page; quotes are the fragments it returned.
